Calico.fact: Calico (; in British usage since 1505) is a heavy plain-woven textile made from unbleached, and often not fully processed, cotton.

Calico.question: Calico (; in British usage since _____) is a heavy plain-woven textile made from unbleached, and often not fully processed, cotton
Calico.fact: Calico (; in British usage since 1505) is a heavy plain-woven textile made from unbleached, and often not fully processed, cotton.

Caligula.question: The _____ was Roman emperor from AD 37 to 41.
Caligula.fact: Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus (31 August AD 12 – 24 January AD 41), also called Gaius or Caligula (), was the third Roman emperor, ruling from AD 37 until his assassination in AD 41.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He was the son of the Roman general _____ and Agrippina the Elder, Augustus' granddaughter, members of the first ruling family of the Roman Empire
Caligula.fact: Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus (31 August AD 12 – 24 January AD 41), also called Gaius or Caligula (), was the third Roman emperor, ruling from AD 37 until his assassination in AD 41. He was the son of the Roman general Germanicus and Agrippina the Elder, Augustus' granddaughter, members of the first ruling family of the Roman Empire.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He was born two years before _____ became emperor
Caligula.fact: He was born two years before Tiberius became emperor. Germanicus died in Antioch in AD 19, and Agrippina returned with her six children to Rome, where she became entangled in a bitter feud with Emperor Tiberius, who was Germanicus' biological uncle and adoptive father.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Gaius accompanied his father, mother and siblings on campaign in _____, at little more than four or five years old
Caligula.fact: Gaius accompanied his father, mother and siblings on campaign in Germania, at little more than four or five years old.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He began the construction of two aqueducts in Rome: the _____ and the Anio Novus
Caligula.fact: He began the construction of two aqueducts in Rome: the Aqua Claudia and the Anio Novus.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: During his reign, the empire annexed the client kingdom of _____ as a province
Caligula.fact: During his reign, the empire annexed the client kingdom of Mauretania as a province.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He had to abandon an attempted invasion of _____, and the installation of his statue in the Temple in Jerusalem
Caligula.fact: He had to abandon an attempted invasion of Britain, and the installation of his statue in the Temple in Jerusalem.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: At least some of the conspirators might have planned this as an opportunity to restore the _____ and aristocratic privileges
Caligula.fact: At least some of the conspirators might have planned this as an opportunity to restore the Roman Republic and aristocratic privileges.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Germanicus was a grandson of _____, and Agrippina was the daughter of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Julia the Elder, making her the granddaughter of Augustus
Caligula.fact: Germanicus was a grandson of Mark Antony, and Agrippina was the daughter of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Julia the Elder, making her the granddaughter of Augustus.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: At the age of two or three, he accompanied his father, _____, on campaigns in the north of Germania
Caligula.fact: Germanicus was a grandson of Mark Antony, and Agrippina was the daughter of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Julia the Elder, making her the granddaughter of Augustus. At the age of two or three, he accompanied his father, Germanicus, on campaigns in the north of Germania.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Germanicus was a respected, immensely popular figure among his troops and Roman civilians of every class, and was widely expected to eventually succeed his uncle _____ as emperor
Caligula.fact: Germanicus was a respected, immensely popular figure among his troops and Roman civilians of every class, and was widely expected to eventually succeed his uncle Tiberius as emperor.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: A few months later, _____ was despatched to tour Rome's allies and provinces with his family
Caligula.fact: Germanicus was a respected, immensely popular figure among his troops and Roman civilians of every class, and was widely expected to eventually succeed his uncle Tiberius as emperor. A few months later, Germanicus was despatched to tour Rome's allies and provinces with his family.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Somewhere en route, _____ contracted what proved to be a fatal illness
Caligula.fact: A few months later, Germanicus was despatched to tour Rome's allies and provinces with his family. Somewhere en route, Germanicus contracted what proved to be a fatal illness.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He lingered awhile, and died at _____, Syria, in AD 19, aged 33, convinced that he had been poisoned by the provincial governor, Gnaius Calpurnius Piso
Caligula.fact: He lingered awhile, and died at Antioch, Syria, in AD 19, aged 33, convinced that he had been poisoned by the provincial governor, Gnaius Calpurnius Piso.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Many believed that he had been killed at the behest of _____, as a potential rival
Caligula.fact: Many believed that he had been killed at the behest of Tiberius, as a potential rival. Agrippina made no secret of her imperial ambitions for herself and her sons, and in consequence, her relations with Tiberius rapidly deteriorated.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Agrippina made no secret of her imperial ambitions for herself and her sons, and in consequence, her relations with _____ rapidly deteriorated
Caligula.fact: Many believed that he had been killed at the behest of Tiberius, as a potential rival. Agrippina made no secret of her imperial ambitions for herself and her sons, and in consequence, her relations with Tiberius rapidly deteriorated.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Germanicus was cremated, and his ashes were taken to Rome, escorted by his wife and children, _____ guards, civilian mourners and senators, then placed in the Mausoleum of Augustus
Caligula.fact: Germanicus was cremated, and his ashes were taken to Rome, escorted by his wife and children, Praetorian guards, civilian mourners and senators, then placed in the Mausoleum of Augustus.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He forbade _____ to remarry, for fear that a remarriage would serve her personal ambition, and introduce yet another threat to himself
Caligula.fact: Caligula lived with his mother Agrippina in Rome, in a milieu very different from that of his earlier years. Agrippina made no secret of her imperial ambitions for herself and her sons, and in consequence, her relations with Tiberius rapidly deteriorated.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: After her death two years later, he was sent to live with his paternal grandmother _____
Caligula.fact: After her death two years later, he was sent to live with his paternal grandmother Antonia Minor.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He was befriended by _____' Praetorian prefect, Naevius Sutorius Macro
Caligula.fact: In the year 30, Tiberius had Caligula's brothers, Drusus and Nero, declared public enemies by the Senate, and exiled. Caligula and his three sisters remained in Italy as hostages of Tiberius, kept under close watch.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Macro had been active in the downfall of _____, his ambitious and manipulative predecessor in office, and was a trusted communicant between the emperor, and his senate in Rome
Caligula.fact: Macro had been active in the downfall of Sejanus, his ambitious and manipulative predecessor in office, and was a trusted communicant between the emperor, and his senate in Rome.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: At the time, _____ seemed to be in good health, and likely to survive until Gemellus' majority
Caligula.fact: In 35, Tiberius named Caligula as joint heir with Tiberius' grandson, Gemellus, who was Caligula's junior by seven years and not yet an adult. At the time, Tiberius seemed to be in good health, and likely to survive until Gemellus' majority.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He probably owed his life to that and, as all the ancient sources agree, to _____
Caligula.fact: He probably owed his life to that and, as all the ancient sources agree, to Macro.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Philo and _____, the latter a Romano-Jewish writer who served Vespasian a generation later, describe Tiberius' death as natural
Caligula.fact: Philo and Josephus, the latter a Romano-Jewish writer who served Vespasian a generation later, describe Tiberius' death as natural.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: His leadership of the domus _____ ("Caesar's household") as its sole heir and pater familias was ratified by the senate, who acclaimed him imperator two days after the death of Tiberius
Caligula.fact: His leadership of the domus Caesaris ("Caesar's household") as its sole heir and pater familias was ratified by the senate, who acclaimed him imperator two days after the death of Tiberius.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The will was annulled with the standard justification that _____ must have been insane when he composed it, incapable of good judgment
Caligula.fact: Tiberius' will named two heirs, Caligula and Gemellus, but the latter was still a minor, and could not hold any kind of office. The will was annulled with the standard justification that Tiberius must have been insane when he composed it, incapable of good judgment.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Every citizen in _____ was given 150 sesterces, and heads of households twice that amount
Caligula.fact: Every citizen in Rome was given 150 sesterces, and heads of households twice that amount.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Building projects on the _____ hill and elsewhere were also announced, which would have been the largest of these expenditures
Caligula.fact: Building projects on the Palatine hill and elsewhere were also announced, which would have been the largest of these expenditures.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: even-handed" rule earned him goodwill throughout the _____
Caligula.fact: even-handed" rule earned him goodwill throughout the Empire.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Caligula took up his first consulship on _____ July, two months after his succession
Caligula.fact: Caligula took up his first consulship on 1 July, two months after his succession. Caligula refused it, protesting his youth, until 21 September 37.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He accepted all titles and honours offered him except pater patriae ("father of the fatherland"), which had been conferred on _____
Caligula.fact: He accepted all titles and honours offered him except pater patriae ("father of the fatherland"), which had been conferred on Augustus. He granted his sisters and his grandmother Antonia Minor extraordinary privileges, normally reserved for the Vestals, and female priesthoods of the deified Augustus; their powers were entirely ceremonial, not executive, but their names were included in the standard formulas used in the senate house to invoke divine blessings on debates and proceedings, and th...

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He commemorated his own father, _____, with portraits on coinage, adopted his name, and renamed the month of September after him
Caligula.fact: He commemorated his own father, Germanicus, with portraits on coinage, adopted his name, and renamed the month of September after him.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: By late _____, their emperor had recovered, and embarked on what might have been a purge of suspected opponents or conspirators
Caligula.fact: By late October, their emperor had recovered, and embarked on what might have been a purge of suspected opponents or conspirators.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Suetonius offers several versions of _____' death
Caligula.fact: Gemellus, Caligula's adopted son and heir, now 18 years old and legally adult, was also disposed of. Suetonius offers several versions of Gemellus' death.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: She was deified and renamed _____ ("All Goddesses"); the first mortal woman in Roman history to be made a diva (goddess of state)
Caligula.fact: She was deified and renamed Panthea ("All Goddesses"); the first mortal woman in Roman history to be made a diva (goddess of state).

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In chariot races, he supported the _____, and personally drove his favourite racehorse, Incitatus ("Speedy") as a member of the Green faction
Caligula.fact: In chariot races, he supported the Greens, and personally drove his favourite racehorse, Incitatus ("Speedy") as a member of the Green faction.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Most of _____'s aristocracy would have found this an unprecedented, unacceptable indignity for any of their number, let alone their emperor
Caligula.fact: Most of Rome's aristocracy would have found this an unprecedented, unacceptable indignity for any of their number, let alone their emperor.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Provincial citizens were liable for direct payment of taxes used to fund the military, a payment from which _____ were exempt
Caligula.fact: Provincial citizens were liable for direct payment of taxes used to fund the military, a payment from which Italians were exempt.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Dio and _____ describe these taxes as "shameful": some were remarkably petty
Caligula.fact: Dio and Suetonius describe these taxes as "shameful": some were remarkably petty.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Citizens of provincial _____ lost their previous tax exemptions
Caligula.fact: Citizens of provincial Italy lost their previous tax exemptions.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Even then, the revenue was nowhere near enough, and the imposition was deeply resented by _____'s commoners
Caligula.fact: Even then, the revenue was nowhere near enough, and the imposition was deeply resented by Rome's commoners.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Josephus claims that this led to riotous protests at the _____
Caligula.fact: Josephus claims that this led to riotous protests at the Circus.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Similar allegations would be made in the future against _____ and Elagabalus
Caligula.fact: Similar allegations would be made in the future against Commodus and Elagabalus.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Winterling describes the families who occupied these rooms as hostage, under the supervision of the _____; some paid up willingly, some reluctantly, but all paid
Caligula.fact: Winterling describes the families who occupied these rooms as hostage, under the supervision of the Praetorians; some paid up willingly, some reluctantly, but all paid.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The military remained responsible for all tax collection, and the tax on prostitution continued up to the reign of _____
Caligula.fact: The military remained responsible for all tax collection, and the tax on prostitution continued up to the reign of Severus Alexander.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: His base metal coinage was struck in _____
Caligula.fact: It seems that Caligula initially produced his precious coins from Lugdunum (now Lyon, France), like his predecessors, then moved the mint to Rome in 37–38, although it is possible that this move occurred later, under Nero. His base metal coinage was struck in Rome.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He also made a sesterce celebrating the _____ cohorts as a mean to give them the bequest of Tiberius at the beginning of his reign
Caligula.fact: He also made a sesterce celebrating the Praetorian cohorts as a mean to give them the bequest of Tiberius at the beginning of his reign.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Caligula minted a quadrans, a small bronze coin, to mark the abolition of the ducentesima, a _____ tax on sales
Caligula.fact: Caligula minted a quadrans, a small bronze coin, to mark the abolition of the ducentesima, a 0.5% tax on sales.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In the city of Rome, he completed the temple of _____ and the reconstruction of the theatre of Pompey
Caligula.fact: In the city of Rome, he completed the temple of Augustus and the reconstruction of the theatre of Pompey.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He is said to have built a bridge between the temple of Castor and Pollux and the _____
Caligula.fact: He is said to have built a bridge between the temple of Castor and Pollux and the Capitol.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He built a large racetrack, now known as the _____ of Gaius and Nero
Caligula.fact: He built a large racetrack, now called the Circus of Gaius and Nero.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In its central spine he incorporated an _____ obelisk, now known as the Vatican obelisk, which he had brought by sea on a gigantic, purpose-built ship, which used 120,000 modi of lentils as ballast
Caligula.fact: In its central spine he incorporated an Egyptian obelisk, now called the Vatican obelisk, which he had brought by sea on a gigantic, purpose-built ship, which used 120,000 modi of lentils as ballast.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He intended to dig a canal through the _____ of Corinth in Greece and sent a chief centurion to survey the site
Caligula.fact: He intended to dig a canal through the Isthmus of Corinth in Greece and sent a chief centurion to survey the site.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He accused them of servility, treachery and hypocrisy in voting honours to _____ and Sejanus while they lived, and rescinding those honours once their recipients were safely dead
Caligula.fact: He accused them of servility, treachery and hypocrisy in voting honours to Tiberius and Sejanus while they lived, and rescinding those honours once their recipients were safely dead.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Apparently seeking to please him and assure his safety, the _____ proposed that his senatorial chair be raised "on a high platform even in the very Senate house"
Caligula.fact: When the senate returned next day, they seemed to confirm his suspicions, and voted him a special guard of armed pretorians to protect him and guard his statues. Apparently seeking to please him and assure his safety, the Senate proposed that his senatorial chair be raised "on a high platform even in the very Senate house".

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: A two-day ceremonial was performed, with offerings to the sea-god _____ and Invidia (Envy), and a satisfactory result, in that the sea remained completely calm
Caligula.fact: A two-day ceremonial was performed, with offerings to the sea-god Neptune and Invidia (Envy), and a satisfactory result, in that the sea remained completely calm.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The bridge was said to rival the _____ king Xerxes' pontoon bridge across the Hellespont
Caligula.fact: The bridge was said to rival the Persian king Xerxes' pontoon bridge across the Hellespont.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The two groups had settled throughout the _____ and Judaea was ruled as a Roman client kingdom
Caligula.fact: The two groups had settled throughout the Roman Empire and Judaea was ruled as a Roman client kingdom.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: They settled in Egypt following its conquest by _____, and remained there after its conquest by Rome
Caligula.fact: They settled in Egypt following its conquest by Macedonian Greeks, and remained there after its conquest by Rome.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: While the _____ held citizen status, Alexandrian Jews were classified as mere settlers, with no statutory or citizen rights other than those granted them by their Roman governors
Caligula.fact: While the Alexandrian Greeks held citizen status, Alexandrian Jews were classified as mere settlers, with no statutory or citizen rights other than those granted them by their Roman governors.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The Greeks feared that official recognition of _____ as citizens would undermine their own status and privilege
Caligula.fact: While the Alexandrian Greeks held citizen status, Alexandrian Jews were classified as mere settlers, with no statutory or citizen rights other than those granted them by their Roman governors. The Greeks feared that official recognition of Jews as citizens would undermine their own status and privilege.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Flaccus responded by declaring the Jews "foreigners and aliens", and expelled them from all but one of _____'s five districts, where they lived under dreadful conditions
Caligula.fact: In 38, Caligula sent Agrippa to Alexandria unannounced to check on Flaccus. Flaccus responded by declaring the Jews "foreigners and aliens", and expelled them from all but one of Alexandria's five districts, where they lived under dreadful conditions.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Philo gives an account of various atrocities inflicted on _____'s Jews within and around this ghetto by the city's Greek population
Caligula.fact: In 38, Caligula sent Agrippa to Alexandria unannounced to check on Flaccus. Flaccus responded by declaring the Jews "foreigners and aliens", and expelled them from all but one of Alexandria's five districts, where they lived under dreadful conditions.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In 39, _____ accused his uncle Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, of planning a rebellion against Roman rule with the help of Parthia
Caligula.fact: In 39, Agrippa accused his uncle Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, of planning a rebellion against Roman rule with the help of Parthia. Herod Antipas confessed, Caligula exiled him, and Agrippa was rewarded with his territories.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Riots again erupted in _____ in 40 between Jews and Greeks, when Jews who refused to venerate the emperor as a god were accused of dishonouring him
Caligula.fact: Riots again erupted in Alexandria in 40 between Jews and Greeks, when Jews who refused to venerate the emperor as a god were accused of dishonouring him.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In the _____ city of Jamnia, resident Greeks built a shoddy, sub-standard altar to the Imperial cult, intending to provoke a reaction from the Jews; they immediately tore it down
Caligula.fact: In the Judaean city of Jamnia, resident Greeks built a shoddy, sub-standard altar to the Imperial cult, intending to provoke a reaction from the Jews; they immediately tore it down.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In May of _____, Philo accompanied a deputation of Alexandrian Jews and Greeks to Caligula, and a second deputation after 31 August that year, during the worst of the Alexandrian riots
Caligula.fact: In May of 40, Philo accompanied a deputation of Alexandrian Jews and Greeks to Caligula, and a second deputation after 31 August that year, during the worst of the Alexandrian riots.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The ethnically Greek population of _____ had already made their loyalty to the new emperor clear, with displays of his image as focus for his cult
Caligula.fact: The ethnically Greek population of Alexandria had already made their loyalty to the new emperor clear, with displays of his image as focus for his cult.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The Governor of Syria, _____, ordered a statue from Sidon, then postponed its installation for as long he could, rather than risk a serious Jewish rebellion
Caligula.fact: The Governor of Syria, Publius Petronius, ordered a statue from Sidon, then postponed its installation for as long he could, rather than risk a serious Jewish rebellion.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Very similar rumours attended _____'s last days, up to his assassination and very much to his discredit
Caligula.fact: Very similar rumours attended Julius Caesar's last days, up to his assassination and very much to his discredit.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: It was the main source of _____'s grain supply, and was administered by members of the equestrian order, directly responsible to the ruling emperor
Caligula.fact: It was the main source of Italy's grain supply, and was administered by members of the equestrian order, directly responsible to the ruling emperor.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Modern historians, however, suppose that he had a valid political reason for his _____ operation, and might even have been successful with that
Caligula.fact: He might have meant to follow the paths of his father and grandfather, and attack the Germanic tribes along the upper Rhine; but according to ancient historians he was ill-prepared, and retreated in a panic. Modern historians, however, suppose that he had a valid political reason for his Germanic operation, and might even have been successful with that.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: But the exact locations and enemies of his campaign cannot be determined; possibilities include the Chatti in and around modern-day Hesse or the Suebi east of the _____
Caligula.fact: He might have meant to follow the paths of his father and grandfather, and attack the Germanic tribes along the upper Rhine; but according to ancient historians he was ill-prepared, and retreated in a panic. But the exact locations and enemies of his campaign cannot be determined; possibilities include the Chatti in and around modern-day Hesse or the Suebi east of the Upper Rhine.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: He announced that he would only be returning "to those who wanted him back"; to the "_____ and the People"; he did not mention the Senate or senators, of whom he had grown increasingly mistrustful
Caligula.fact: He announced that he would only be returning "to those who wanted him back"; to the "Equestrians and the People"; he did not mention the Senate or senators, of whom he had grown increasingly mistrustful.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: In an event that Suetonius describes as "well known", a Praetorian gentleman, nodding off to sleep after a gladiator match, woke to find that he had bought 13 gladiators for the vastly over-inflated s
Caligula.fact: In an event that Suetonius describes as "well known", a Praetorian gentleman, nodding off to sleep after a gladiator match, woke to find that he had bought 13 gladiators for the vastly over-inflated sum of 9 million sesterces.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Beyond mutinies, it may have simply been that _____ chieftains acceded to Rome's demands, removing any justification for war
Caligula.fact: Beyond mutinies, it may have simply been that British chieftains acceded to Rome's demands, removing any justification for war. Alternatively, it could have been merely a training and scouting mission or a short expedition to accept the surrender of the British chieftain Adminius.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Alternatively, it could have been merely a training and scouting mission or a short expedition to accept the surrender of the _____ chieftain Adminius
Caligula.fact: Beyond mutinies, it may have simply been that British chieftains acceded to Rome's demands, removing any justification for war. Alternatively, it could have been merely a training and scouting mission or a short expedition to accept the surrender of the British chieftain Adminius.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Its ruler, _____ of Mauretania, was a noble descendant of Juba II, popular, extremely wealthy and with a reputation as "feckless and incompetent"
Caligula.fact: Its ruler, Ptolemy of Mauretania, was a noble descendant of Juba II, popular, extremely wealthy and with a reputation as "feckless and incompetent". Ptolemy failed to deal effectively with an uprising and was removed.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: His removal proved unpopular enough in _____ to provoke an uprising
Caligula.fact: Its ruler, Ptolemy of Mauretania, was a noble descendant of Juba II, popular, extremely wealthy and with a reputation as "feckless and incompetent". His removal proved unpopular enough in Mauretania to provoke an uprising.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Rome divided Mauretania into two provinces, _____ and Mauretania Caesariensis, separated by the river Malua
Caligula.fact: Rome divided Mauretania into two provinces, Mauretania Tingitana and Mauretania Caesariensis, separated by the river Malua.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: The first known equestrian governor of the joint provinces was Marcus Fadius Celer Flavianus, in office in _____
Caligula.fact: The first known equestrian governor of the joint provinces was Marcus Fadius Celer Flavianus, in office in 44. Details on the Mauretanian events of 39–44 are lost, including an entire chapter by Dio on the annexation.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Details on the _____ events of 39–44 are lost, including an entire chapter by Dio on the annexation
Caligula.fact: Details on the Mauretanian events of 39–44 are lost, including an entire chapter by Dio on the annexation. The rebellion of Tacfarinas had shown how exposed Africa Proconsularis was to its west and how the Mauretanian client kings were unable to provide protection to the province, and it is thus possible that Caligula's expansion was a prudent and ultimately successful response to potential future threats.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Coin issues of the official Roman mint, dated to the early 20s BC, show _____ as Apollo, Jupiter and Neptune
Caligula.fact: Coin issues of the official Roman mint, dated to the early 20s BC, show Octavian as Apollo, Jupiter and Neptune.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: As Gradel observes, no _____ was ever prosecuted for sacrificing to his emperor
Caligula.fact: As Gradel observes, no Roman was ever prosecuted for sacrificing to his emperor.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: When Pausanias visited the still-unfinished temple a century later, its cult statue was of _____
Caligula.fact: Caligula wished to take over or share the half-finished but splendid Temple of Apollo in Greek Didyma for his own cult. When Pausanias visited the still-unfinished temple a century later, its cult statue was of Apollo.

Caligula.subject: Business & Economy
Caligula.question: Most modern scholarship agrees that if such a temple existed, it was probably on the _____
Caligula.fact: Most modern scholarship agrees that if such a temple existed, it was probably on the Palatine.
